safety.text: Version 0.17.0-alpha.17: new battery and heating-buffer outputs are disabled and unmapped by default. Heat-pump modes are advice only, without an external mode write. Before enabling any real output, stop competing output scripts and commission it under supervision. Before returning to scripts, disable the master release and wait until all OutputOwned states are false. Host or driver failure requires independent device-side protection; an EMS process cannot guarantee a final stop after a host crash.

multiWallboxAlphaArmed.label: Arm ALPHA control for all released wallboxes + DHW (competing output scripts stopped)

houseConnectionHelp.text: The adapter derives one common working limit (fuse minus reserve) for wallboxes and DHW. Legacy separate limits remain readable only for migration.

par14aActiveHigh.label: Binary contact: true/1 means limitation active

options.label: Calculate EMS minimum from configured participants
Complete AC power including relevant auxiliary loads

par14aCalculationHelp.text: Count the agreed permanently assigned EMS devices, not connected cars. Heat pumps and cooling systems are each grouped; each electrical load including auxiliaries must be entered once. Standalone heaters are not additional participants. Only devices/groups above 4200 W count. Standard: 4200 + (n-1)*GZF*4200 W. With WP/cooling above 11000 W: max(0.4*P_WP,0.4*P_cooling) + (n-1)*GZF*4200 W. Result: Control.GridOperatorCalculation_JSON after saving. Participant calculation does not prove registration or complete AC coverage; group net accounting must be selected and configured separately.

par14aGzfOverrideEnabled.label: Advanced: use a non-standard GZF table (shown as deviation)

par14aGzfFactors.label: Non-standard GZF table (count 9 means 9 or more)

par14aScopeHelp.text: Existing fixed limits and signal mappings remain unchanged in legacy gross mode. Group net mode applies only to an explicitly declared binary-contact group and complete AC boundary. Configured LPC inputs block the new mode pending a verified official interface contract. External total budgets are used directly and never multiplied by GZF.

par14aAccountingMode.label: Grid-operator accounting mode

options.label: Declared group net import with measured own supply

par14aAccountingMode.help: Group net accounting requires an explicitly declared participant group and complete AC measurement boundary. Existing settings remain in conservative gross mode until you select the new mode. This does not enable Master Control or arm any output. Configured LPC inputs block the new mode until their official interface contract is verified.

options.label: Complete site AC import and export at the declared boundary

par14aAccountingSiteHelp.text: The existing grid import/export mappings must be separate nonnegative watt measurements for the complete declared site boundary. The site balance already contains PV, CHP and storage effects; these are never added a second time. Do not use a partial circuit or an inverter/DC reading as whole-site proof.

par14aAccountingTimeHelp.text: Fresh valid but asynchronous measurements use the shared gross ceiling without own-supply credit. Original timestamps remain unchanged; net attribution is unknown. Stale, bad-quality, incomplete or unacknowledged sources remain blocked. The timestamp-span bound applies to own-supply credit, not to synchronisation of devices.

par14aStorageCoverage.label: Storage coverage within the AC boundary

options.label: No electricity storage within this AC boundary
All storage covered by complete signed AC meters
Complete AC power including relevant auxiliary loads

par14aStorageHelp.text: Declare every storage AC meter and its actual sign convention. Battery/DC telemetry does not replace AC measurements. Unknown storage coverage blocks group net accounting. Observed discharge is diagnosed separately and cannot fund additional discretionary charging or heating.

par14aParticipantMeterHelp.text: For group net mode, bind every participant to its original complete AC measurement, including heat-pump auxiliary or emergency heaters. A controlled wallbox or battery requires its own complete meter. Passive participants may share one complete aggregate meter only when its coverage is declared once without overlapping sub-meters. Standalone DHW or heating-buffer heaters are not additional section-14a participants. Empty output binding means measured participant without EMS control. Missing bindings or incomplete coverage block positive group-budget grants.

par14aControlledBatteryHelp.text: For an EMS-controlled multi-head SunEnergy battery, bind the storage participant to Battery and enter @controlled-battery-ac as its power data point, W and complete AC scope. This token represents the charging sum of all selected controlled heads; it is not an ioBroker state and creates no extra subscription. Every selected head must appear in the storage AC table with its original grid.GP measurement, W, complete AC scope and positive-discharge sign convention. Missing or mismatched head coverage blocks the group budget; DC batteryPower values cannot replace it.

measurementHelp.text: Required for normal operation: PV power and either grid import/export or an equivalent mapped source. Values are expected in watts. Explicit fields override legacy JSON entries.

bhkwHelp.text: BHKW is recorded separately from PV. The net meter already includes its power: no extra live budget or forecast generation is added. Missing, stale or unacknowledged values remain unknown. Daily energy requires valid counter differences. After decommissioning disable BHKW present.

outsideTemperatureHelp.text: Expected unit: °C. Invalid or unavailable values are ignored; forecast calculations continue with their conservative fallback.

_phaseMeasurementHeader.text: Optional phase measurements for house-connection protection

diagnosticPumpSourcesJson.label: Optional pump sources for passive recording (JSON)
diagnosticPumpSourcesJson.help: Enter a JSON array of up to 32 explicit state IDs for pump request, command and independent feedback, without wildcards. These sources are read for diagnostic recording only; they do not control the pump. The default empty list adds no source mapping. Missing or invalid sources remain unknown and cannot confirm a pump response or run-on.

_priceQuarterHelp.text: Forecast prices and tariff windows use 15-minute intervals. Real-time power control continues at its configured seconds interval. All resulting prices are gross ct/kWh.

_priceMigrationHelp.text: Existing amounts are preserved without automatic reinterpretation. Review whether the fixed energy component, fixed grid fee, energy adders and external grid-fee series are net or gross. This selector applies to these four inputs; exchange prices and the annual tariff have their own basis.

_priceChargingHelp.text: Enable price-based grid charging separately on the Battery tab or each Wallbox tab. The comparison uses the full gross price including energy, adders and grid fees. A fixed energy tariff with time-dependent grid fees also works. Expected usable PV reduces the required grid energy. Without departure time, vehicles account for usable PV over the next 48 h. The price window above (default 24 h) limits grid purchases, not when the car must be full. An enabled departure remains a fixed deadline. Blocks avoid chasing each quarter-hour. Existing master, device and production releases still apply.

options.label: Contract total price with reference grid fee

referenceGridFeeCt.label: Grid fee included in contract price (gross)

_fixedTotalHelp.text: Enter your actual contract price. The energy component is total price minus the included reference grid fee; the applicable grid fee is then added per interval. Both inputs in this mode are always gross. A total price of 0 is not configured.

fixedGridFeeCt.label: Fixed grid fee (dynamic grid fee disabled)

_directExchangeHelp.text: Energy-Charts supplies actual published DE-LU quarter-hour prices in EUR/MWh, always net. The adapter converts the unit and adds VAT once. Unpublished intervals remain missing and cannot authorize price-dependent operation.

priceSwitchHelp.text: An external enable data point overrides its internal switch. Missing or invalid external switch values disable that dynamic source and are reported in diagnostics. Selecting a source alone does not enable it.

_annualTariffHelp.text: Editable example: Avacon 2026, module 3. Confirm prices, eligibility and tariff year against your own agreement. Time windows apply daily in Europe/Berlin, including daylight-saving changes. Each quarter must cover 00:00–24:00 without gaps or overlaps. Use quarter-hour boundaries; split a window at midnight. An expired or incomplete tariff is reported as invalid and cannot authorize price-dependent operation.

wallboxParallelChargingEnabled.label: Parallel wallbox charging
wallboxParallelChargingEnabled.help: Reserve at least 6 A single-phase for each eligible released vehicle below its minimum SoC, subject to house-connection, grid-operator and device limits. Remaining power goes to the preferred vehicle, then to the next automatically ranked vehicles. Target SoC remains binding. When disabled, only one EMS-controlled wallbox charges at a time. This option does not enable Master Control or arm outputs.

wallboxPriority.label: Preferred wallbox (manual selection takes priority)
wallboxPriority.help: Manual priority: 0 = Mii, 1 = EQV, 2 = EQE. In parallel mode, a valid preferred vehicle receives remaining power after the minimum-SoC reservations; other vehicles follow the automatic ranking. In sequential mode, the selected eligible vehicle takes priority over other vehicles, including minimum-SoC charging. Target SoC, safety limits and source/charging eligibility checks always apply.

wallboxCombinedMaxStepA.label: Maximum current step with DHW active

wallboxStopDelayS.label: Delay before stopping on insufficient surplus

wallboxRestartHandoffEnabled.label: Keep an EMS-owned active wallbox running during adapter restart/update

wallboxRestartHandoffTimeoutS.label: Maximum wait for fresh control data after restart
wallboxRestartHandoffTimeoutS.help: At least 900 seconds for startup/history loading; older smaller values use 900 seconds automatically. Final stabilization has its own completion margin.

wallboxRestartHandoffGraceS.label: Protect adopted wallbox from transient zero target

wallboxRestartHandoffSettleS.label: Stable EMS data required before restart handoff completes

wallboxResponseSettleTimeoutS.label: Vehicle response timeout after command acknowledgement
wallboxResponseSettleTimeoutS.help: After a confirmed current or start command, wait for fresh electrical readings before increasing again. Real charger errors and safety limits remain immediate.

wallboxResponseCurrentToleranceA.label: Vehicle response current tolerance
wallboxResponseCurrentToleranceA.help: Tolerance for measured current versus confirmed command. This does not change the charger over-current protection.

phaseSwitchRealDownDelayS.label: Measured budget delay before switching to 1 phase
phaseSwitchRealDownDelayS.help: A continuously valid measured budget below the three-phase minimum qualifies a single-phase request after this delay. Missing or invalid samples cancel the timer. The minimum time between phase changes still applies. Forecast recommendations do not override a qualified real request.

phaseSwitchRealUpDelayS.label: Measured budget delay before switching to 3 phases
phaseSwitchRealUpDelayS.help: A continuously valid measured budget sufficient for three-phase charging qualifies a three-phase request after this delay. Missing or invalid samples cancel the timer. The minimum time between phase changes still applies. Forecast recommendations do not override a qualified real request.

_wb0PriceHelp.text: With valid vehicle SoC, the existing target determines the energy needed. Without SoC, enter the AC energy to add per plug-in session (0 = no price-based grid charging without SoC). Measured charging reduces the remaining session energy; a restart does not reset it. Usable PV is planned first. Without departure time, usable PV over the next 48 h reduces grid demand; sufficient PV tomorrow avoids unnecessary charging tonight. An enabled departure is a fixed deadline. The price window (default 24 h) only limits the search for grid-charging blocks. The price cap is the full gross price including time-dependent grid fees; 0 means no additional cap. User permission, master, device and production releases remain required.

_heatingOutputHelp.text: Independent my-PV controller for the heating buffer; never reuse the DHW actuator. Requires its own setpoint, three measured output powers, connection and buffer temperature. Cooling active, unknown cooling status or manual inhibit blocks heating. Temperature limits do not replace the heater's physical thermostat and safety cut-out.

options.label: SunEnergy standard adapter: 1–3 heads, SoC balancing

batteryHeadCount.label: Number of configured SunEnergy heads
batteryHeadCount.help: Select exactly the heads configured in the standard driver: head 1, heads 1–2 or heads 1–3. Unselected configured heads are not permitted. This setting does not enable battery control.

_batterySunEnergyHeadsHelp.text: The unchanged SunEnergy standard adapter remains the device driver. Set its control mode to Off, with each selected head in local mode LM=1 and manual grid mode MM=0. The EMS writes each heads.N.control.GS directly, never a virtual house-grid signal. GS and GP are positive for discharge and negative for charge; EMS internal power is positive for charge. Fresh per-head rawResponse and online feedback are required. Missing or invalid head data blocks the output and retains the unconfirmed power reserve. Acknowledged GS alone is not physical power feedback.

_batterySunEnergyBalanceHelp.text: SoC balancing prefers lower-SoC heads when charging and higher-SoC heads when discharging. The reported ON pack count weights each head's relative capacity; it is not an online flag. Per-head limits, measured device limits and the shared total budget remain binding. All requested head powers have the same direction: the EMS does not charge one head while discharging another. Exact equality is not guaranteed while power, SoC or availability limits differ.

_batterySunEnergyProfileHelp.text: In this mode the EMS reads SoC (SC), online pack count (ON), actual AC power (GP), device SoC limits and device/model power limits from coherent per-head responses. Separate SoC and DC-power mappings are not used. User targets, permissions and additional power limits remain unchanged. No dynamic BMS charge limit, efficiency or battery temperature is inferred.

_batteryOutputHelp.text: Supervised SunEnergy battery output: choose the exact sunenergyxt500.N.heads.H.control.GS endpoint and its mandatory AC power feedback heads.H.grid.GP (or total.gridPower only with exactly one configured head). Both GS and GP are positive for discharge/export; the EMS inverts GP to internal positive=charge. BP / total.batteryPower is DC telemetry for history/planning and must not replace AC command feedback. The SunEnergy adapter must use controlMode=off, a fresh info.lastUpdate heartbeat and the selected head must confirm online=true, MM=false and LM=true. A direct GS command has no EMS-side protection against a host crash: a device-side watchdog remains necessary for unattended operation.

batteryProductionArmed.label: Arm supervised battery output: GS mapping, signs, driver modes and competing writer checked

batterySetpointId.label: Writable sunenergyxt500.N.heads.H.control.GS (W: positive discharge / negative charge)

batteryAcPowerId.label: Required AC power feedback: selected head grid.GP or single-head total.gridPower (W, positive discharge)

batteryHeartbeatId.label: Fresh driver heartbeat / last successful update

batteryFaultId.label: Optional driver fault state (0 / false = no fault)

batteryTemperatureId.label: Optional battery cell temperature for thermal protection (°C; configured source must be valid)

batteryPowerId.label: Battery DC power for history/planning (BP / total.batteryPower, W; not GS feedback)

batteryPowerSign.label: Legacy DC power convention (never used for GS / AC feedback)

options.label: DC source positive = charge (SunEnergy BP / total.batteryPower)
Online packs from the SunEnergy adapter

batteryPackCapacityKWh.label: Confirmed capacity per equal-sized battery pack
batteryPackCapacityKWh.help: Enter a positive kWh value from the pack documentation. Zero means not specified, not zero-capacity hardware.

_batterySunEnergyCapacityHelp.text: Automatic capacity is the sum of online packs (ON) multiplied by the explicitly entered capacity of one equal-sized pack. ON is an online pack count, not the nominal installed capacity. Confirm the pack size from your device documentation; no default pack size is assumed. Missing or invalid data for any selected head, or a missing pack size, makes automatic capacity unknown and prevents a valid battery forecast. The manual capacity is not used as a silent fallback.

batteryTemperatureMinSocEnabled.label: Use forecast temperature for the minimum SoC

batteryTemperatureForecastId.label: Forecast minimum outside temperature for the upcoming night (°C)

batteryTemperatureForecastMaxAgeH.label: Maximum age of the temperature forecast

batteryTemperatureLowerThresholdC.label: Cold band: forecast below this temperature

batteryTemperatureColdMinSocPct.label: Minimum SoC for the cold band

batteryTemperatureUpperThresholdC.label: Cool band: forecast up to and including this temperature

batteryTemperatureCoolMinSocPct.label: Minimum SoC for the cool band

batteryTemperatureWarmMinSocPct.label: Minimum SoC above the upper temperature threshold

_batteryTemperatureMinSocHelp.text: The daily selection period starts at 20:00 Europe/Berlin. At most one successful selection is made per unchanged source/settings contract and period. Initial activation uses a valid available forecast; a restart preserves a qualified selection for the same period. Defaults: below 0 °C = 30%, from 0 °C through 5 °C = 20%, above 5 °C = 10%. This replaces only the effective EMS minimum SoC; maximum SoC and morning/afternoon/late targets remain unchanged. Use a forecast for the upcoming night: day1 is tomorrow, while day0 is today. The source must be a confirmed, valid numeric value in °C within the configured maximum age. An invalid or missing forecast retains the last valid selection; before the first valid selection, the fixed minimum applies and the fallback is shown. A later valid forecast can complete the current period with its actual selection time. Thresholds must be ordered and all selected reserves must be below the configured maximum SoC. No external SI endpoint is written and no grid-charging or output release is enabled.

batteryPriceChargingEnabled.label: Allow battery grid charging in selected low-price periods

batteryPriceMaxSocPct.label: Maximum SoC from grid charging (PV may charge higher)

batteryPriceMaxCt.label: Maximum total gross price (0 = no cap)

_batteryPriceHelp.text: Opt-in grid charging is scheduled against expected demand, PV, storage losses and later total electricity prices. The extra reserve is in percentage points above the configured minimum SoC, capped by the maximum SoC. The price cap uses the full gross price, including time-dependent grid fees; negative caps are allowed. 0 means no additional price cap, not free electricity. Round-trip efficiency 0 preserves the legacy efficiency per direction. The separate grid-charge maximum SoC does not limit PV charging. Missing prices do not authorize grid charging. Existing master, device and battery production releases remain required.

_batteryFineControlHeader.text: Battery fine control and input checks

batteryFineReserveW.label: PV reserve for battery fine control before heater allocation

_batteryFineReserveHelp.text: Reserves up to this share of actual PV surplus for battery fine control. The effective reserve is capped by available PV, battery charge power and the shared grid-operator budget; without available PV there is no reserve. Existing planned battery charging can require a larger share. This is a power reserve in watts, not an additional SoC reserve or permission to charge from the grid.

batteryTemperatureMaxC.label: Optional battery cell temperature stop limit

_batteryMinimumHelp.text: The 15% minimum applies to new installations only. Existing explicit settings are retained. A minimum of 0% blocks productive discharge; configure an appropriate positive reserve before a supervised test.

heatPumpPowerScope.label: Scope of the electrical power measurement

_heatPumpPowerHelp.text: Select the source unit explicitly: W or kW. ISG register 3680 reports IWS inverter power, not proven total heat-pump consumption including auxiliary heaters and pumps. Select inverter scope for that source unless a separate total measurement is verified. Inverter scope is not complete §14a telemetry. Missing, stale, unacknowledged or bad-quality power remains unknown, never 0 W. Valid measured power is required for SG Ready 3/4 recommendations.

heatPumpConnectionId.label: Optional heat-pump connection status (confirmed true when configured)

_heatPumpFeedbackHelp.text: An empty connection mapping is optional; a configured source must confirm a valid online state. SG Ready feedback must already be decoded to logical state 1, 2, 3 or 4; do not map raw input bits, an unrelated operating status or legacy EMS mode values. Device feedback describes the actual state, not acknowledgement of an EMS command. No command is sent.

heatPumpBufferTemperatureId.label: Heat-pump buffer temperature (empty = configured heating-buffer temperature source)

heatPumpDhwTemperatureId.label: Heat-pump DHW temperature (explicit source; no automatic sensor selection)

_heatPumpPowerValue.label: Validated electrical power (W; unknown remains empty)

heatPumpControlEnabled.label: Participate in EMS recommendations (no external actuator write)

_heatPumpAdviceHelp.text: Recommendations are EMS-owned information, not commands to the heat pump. No ISG mode endpoint is written. Advice uses measured electrical power, buffer/DHW temperatures, PV surplus, the optional shared cheap-price policy and the cooling status configured in Thermal strategy. Independent heat-pump safety and its own temperature control remain authoritative.

_heatPumpSgReadyHelp.text: SG Ready 1 = block; 2 = normal; 3 = raised heating/DHW request; 4 = maximum heating/DHW request. These states are demand levels, not exact watt targets. SG Ready 4 is not a cooling request. Automatic price-based SG Ready 1 blocking is not implemented. Legacy REDUCED = 0 is an internal EMS inhibition recommendation, never SG Ready 1.

heatPumpHeatingTargetC.label: Heating buffer target for heat-pump advice

heatPumpPvBoostOnW.label: PV surplus to enter SG Ready 3 advice

heatPumpPvBoostOffW.label: PV surplus to leave SG Ready 3 advice

heatPumpMaxBoostEnabled.label: Allow SG Ready 4 maximum-demand recommendation (heating/DHW only)

heatPumpMaxBoostOnW.label: PV surplus to enter SG Ready 4 advice

heatPumpMaxBoostOffW.label: PV surplus to leave SG Ready 4 advice

_heatPumpHysteresisHelp.text: For SG Ready 3 and 4, each entry threshold must be positive and greater than its exit threshold. The maximum-demand recommendation has a separate opt-in and remains a heating/DHW request. Safety blocks, unavailable sources and loss of price permission can end advice before the normal holding time expires.

_heatPumpKnxHeader.text: 3. Separate KNX heating and cooling boost requests

_heatPumpKnxHelp.text: These are internal request/status states only. There is no KNX output mapping or external write release in this version. Heating boost requests available heating-buffer capacity; a DHW-only SG Ready recommendation does not set the KNX heating flag. Cooling boost is a separate optional request and is never SG Ready 4. Cooling requires valid room, flow and dew-point measurements, confirmed cooling status and measured electrical power. The flow target must respect dew point plus safety margin. Existing heat-pump, FET and dew-point protection remains authoritative.

heatPumpCoolingBoostEnabled.label: Enable separate cooling boost recommendation (internal only)

_heatPumpInterfaceHelp.text: ISG register 4258 selects the input mode: SG Ready and PL/LU interpret the input bits differently. In PL/LU mode, input bits 11 mean a power limit, not SG Ready 4. Decode feedback according to the actual configured interface mode. Register 4259 is not implemented here; its unit/scaling is not confirmed, so no writable power-limit field is offered. SG Ready recommendations do not establish a §14a power limit or prove compliance.

_heatPumpReadOnlyHelp.text: The status rows above are read-only Devices.HeatPump states. They show recommendation and feedback separately and do not enable any heat-pump, KNX or ISG output. Source mappings remain visible while recommendations are disabled, so they can be configured and checked before use.

_thermalSharedHelp.text: Shared cooling information protects the heating-buffer heater and informs heat-pump advice. DHW is a separate thermal circuit. Optional cheap-price heating remains disabled unless explicitly released with a positive combined heater grid-power budget; missing prices are never treated as free energy.

heatingCoolingActiveId.label: Shared cooling active (confirmed true/1 = cooling; false/0 = no cooling)

heatingCoolingHeartbeatId.label: Optional cooling-source heartbeat (fresh epoch-ms timestamp; allows unchanged cooling boolean)

thermalCheapPriceEnabled.label: Allow explicitly budgeted heating at cheap total electricity prices

thermalCheapPriceMaxCt.label: Maximum total electricity price for cheap heating

thermalCheapGridMaxW.label: Maximum shared grid-power budget for cheap heater operation (0 = no grid heating)

thermalCheapFixedTariffAllowed.label: Also allow cheap-price heating with an explicitly configured fixed tariff

wallboxPVImportToleranceW.label: Shared PV wallbox grid-import tolerance
wallboxPVImportToleranceW.help: Shared maximum allowance above the grid target for a running charger, including minimum-SoC charging; 0 disables it. New one-amp steps keep a 20 W admission margin below this setting, confirmed current may use the full setting. No extra allowance per vehicle or for cold starts, price charging or hard limits. Mandatory charging and unrelated house loads can still cause higher total grid import.

advancedHelp.text: Migration only: explicit fields on the normal tabs override matching legacy JSON entries. Unchanged JSON entries remain active so updates do not lose existing mappings.

legacyCurrentHelp.text: The legacy free-current values below are used only when direct phase-current or phase-power measurements are unavailable.
